config.title: Compound Component (Tabs)

intro.title: Compound Component (Tabs)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Tabs component using Angular's compound component pattern. You'll create a parent Tabs component that manages the active tab state and child Tab components that display individual tab content. The core concept involves using content projection with <ng-content> and @ContentChildren to let components work together as a single unit. You'll implement this with TypeScript for type safety and Angular's component decorators for structure. By the end, you'll understand how to design flexible UI components where the parent and children share functionality seamlessly.
intro.usecase: The compound component pattern is essential for building reusable, complex UI elements in real-world Angular applications. You'll see this pattern in dashboard interfaces where tabbed panels organize different data views, in e-commerce product pages with tabs for descriptions/reviews/specifications, and in settings panels with categorized options. This approach allows developers to create flexible tab systems where content and behavior can be customized while maintaining consistent structure and state management. Mastering compound components helps you build maintainable enterprise applications with sophisticated user interfaces.

objectives: Construct a tab container component with content projection slots for tab headers and panels
Implement a tab header component that displays clickable tab labels
Configure a tab panel component to conditionally render content based on active state
Integrate tab components using Angular's ContentChildren decorator to manage child relationships
Bind click events on tab headers to control which panel becomes active
Initialize and manipulate the active tab state using Angular's lifecycle hooks
Render a complete tab interface with proper visual feedback for the active tab

steps.title: Import Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, and ContentChild decorators from @angular/core
steps.instruction: Import Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, and ContentChild from '@angular/core' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple decorators from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core decorators
import { Component, Input } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import the required Angular core decorators here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core decorators needed for creating compound components are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, and ContentChild are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required decorators, but need all five: Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, and ContentChild.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, and ContentChild from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main Tabs component structure
steps.instruction: Create a Tabs component class with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from Angular core to define a component. The template can be empty for now.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter, ContentChild } from '@angular/core';

// Create the Tabs component class with @Component decorator and empty template here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tabs component class is defined with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
successCriteria: The Tabs component class is created with @Component decorator, a selector, and an empty template string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @Component decorator with a selector and an empty template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure is incomplete. Check that you've defined a class with @Component decorator and an empty template.

steps.title: Create the Tab component structure
steps.instruction: Create a new Angular component class named Tab with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.hint: Add a new class called Tab below your existing Tabs component. Use the @Component decorator with an empty template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Tab component class defined alongside the Tabs component.
successCriteria: A Tab component class is created with the @Component decorator and an empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a class named Tab with the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component wasn't created correctly. Check that you have a class named Tab with @Component decorator.

steps.title: Add activeTabIndex state to Tabs component
steps.instruction: Inside the Tabs component class, add a public property named activeTabIndex with a type of number and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration like 'activeTabIndex: number = 0;' inside the Tabs class body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component will have internal state to track which tab is currently active, starting with the first tab (index 0).
successCriteria: The Tabs class contains a property named activeTabIndex of type number initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a property named activeTabIndex with type number and initialized it to 0 inside the Tabs class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The activeTabIndex property is missing or incorrect. Add 'activeTabIndex: number = 0;' inside the Tabs class.

steps.title: Add tab selection handler to Tabs component
steps.instruction: Inside the Tabs component class, add a method named selectTab that takes a number parameter (index) and updates the activeTabIndex property with that value.
steps.hint: Define a method with the signature selectTab(index: number): void and set this.activeTabIndex = index inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component now has a selectTab method that can update the active tab index.
successCriteria: The Tabs component contains a selectTab method that accepts a number parameter and assigns it to activeTabIndex.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a method, but check that it takes a number parameter and updates activeTabIndex correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectTab method is missing or doesn't update activeTabIndex as required.

steps.title: Add ContentChild to access Tab components in Tabs
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component class, add a ContentChild property to reference the projected Tab components. Use the ContentChild decorator imported earlier.
steps.hint: Use @ContentChild(Tab) to declare a property that will hold a reference to the first Tab component projected into Tabs.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component will have a property decorated with @ContentChild that can access the Tab components projected into it.
successCriteria: Tabs component contains a property decorated with @ContentChild(Tab) that references Tab components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the ContentChild decorator correctly. Check that you've imported ContentChild and are applying it to a property with the Tab type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ContentChild property wasn't added correctly. Remember to use @ContentChild(Tab) before a property declaration in the Tabs class.

steps.title: Add tab header structure to Tabs template
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component template, add a <div> element with *ngFor to iterate through tabs and display each tab header as a clickable button.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor to loop through the tabs array. Each button should display the tab's title and call the selectTab method when clicked.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: ngFor loop in Angular template
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component template now contains a navigation structure with buttons for each tab header.
successCriteria: The Tabs template includes a <div> with *ngFor that iterates through tabs and displays clickable buttons with tab titles.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your template includes both the *ngFor directive and clickable buttons that display tab titles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required tab header structure. Add a <div> with *ngFor to iterate through tabs and create buttons for each tab header.

steps.title: Wire tab headers to selection handler
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component template, add a click event binding to each button that calls the selectTab method with the current index.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="selectTab(i)" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: wiring a button click to a handler
<button (click)="handleClick(index)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The tab headers will now respond to clicks and trigger the selection handler.
successCriteria: Each button in the template has a (click) event binding that calls selectTab(i).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure each button has the (click)="selectTab(i)" event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tab headers aren't properly wired to the selection handler. Check that you've added the click event binding to each button.

steps.title: Add active tab styling to Tabs template
steps.instruction: Add an ngClass binding to the button element in the Tabs template to apply an 'active' CSS class when the current tab index matches activeTabIndex.
steps.hint: Use [ngClass] with an object expression like {'active': i === activeTabIndex}. This will add the 'active' class conditionally.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional class binding in Angular
<button [ngClass]="{'highlighted': isSelected}">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element in the Tabs template now has an ngClass binding that conditionally applies the 'active' class based on the activeTabIndex.
successCriteria: The button element includes [ngClass] binding with an object expression that checks if i equals activeTabIndex.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the ngClass binding might be incomplete. Make sure it compares the index i with activeTabIndex.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngClass binding is missing or incorrect. The active class should be applied only when the tab index matches activeTabIndex.

steps.title: Add tab content projection to Tabs template
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component template, add an ng-content element after the tab headers to project the content of the active Tab component.
steps.hint: Use ng-content with a selector attribute to target the active tab's content. You'll need to add it inside the template after the existing div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component template now includes an ng-content element that will project the content of the active tab when Tab components are used as children.
successCriteria: The Tabs component template contains an ng-content element with a selector attribute after the tab headers.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you added ng-content with a selector attribute in the Tabs template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs template still needs an ng-content element to project the active tab's content. Try adding it after the tab headers.
